script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. MODERN APARTMENT - NIGHT

Our HERO, JASON, (late 20s, slightly disheveled, dressed in a rumpled shirt and sweatpants) sits on the couch in his dimly lit living room, staring at a blank laptop screen. He takes another sip from a bottle of beer and lets out a frustrated sigh.

JASON: (to himself) This is it. The big break. The chance to prove myself. And what do I do? Squander it with a half-baked script that's going nowhere.

Suddenly, there's a knock at the door. Jason hesitates, then stands up, taking a deep breath to steady himself.

INT. MODERN APARTMENT - ENTRANCEWAY - NIGHT

Jason opens the door to reveal his best friend, SARAH (early 30s, sharp, confident, dressed in a stylish blazer and pants) holding a takeout bag.

SARAH: Hey, I brought you some dinner. I figured you could use a good meal after your all-nighter.

JASON: (surprised) Thanks, Sarah. That's really nice of you.

SARAH: (smiling) No problem. Now, what's going on? You look like you've seen a ghost.

Jason hesitates, then takes a deep breath, explaining his writing woes to Sarah.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Two days later, Jason and Sarah sit at a table in a bustling coffee shop. Jason's face is etched with determination, while Sarah listens intently, taking notes on a pad of paper.

SARAH: (leaning in) So, what if we approached this from a different angle? What if instead of writing a script, you wrote a business plan for a startup related to the film industry?

JASON: (surprised) A startup? Like, what kind of business?

SARAH: (grinning) I've got a few ideas, but I want to hear what you come up with.

INT. MODERN APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jason spends the next few nights holed up in his apartment, brainstorming ideas for his new business. He researchs the film industry, studies market trends, and even reaches out to industry professionals for advice.

INT. COWORKING SPACE - DAY

A few weeks later, Jason sits at a long table in a bustling coworking space, surrounded by other entrepreneurs and freelancers. He's dressed in a sharp suit, looking more confident than ever. Sarah sits across from him, smiling with pride.

JASON: (leaning back) So, we're going to offer script consulting services. We'll help writers develop their ideas, hone their craft, and connect them with industry professionals.

SARAH: (nodding) And we'll also offer workshops and classes to help aspiring writers build a solid foundation in storytelling.

JASON: (grinning) And that's just the beginning. We're going to be the go-to resource for anyone looking to break into the film industry.

INT. FILM STUDIO - DAY

Months later, Jason and Sarah sit in a plush office at a major film studio, surrounded by stacks of scripts and a view of the Hollywood sign. They've made it.

JASON: (looking out at the view) We did it, Sarah.

SARAH: (smiling) Yes, we did.

FADE OUT.

THE END
